body:
Greg starts TermAl on EVERY host with the same two steps. His words, 2026-11-10 15:54Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant in 588693a8 #1278: „robie: - git pull - cargo run --release".

Consequences for every landing and restart:
- **Installed copies are not what runs.** The running binary is cargo's build in target/release from whatever `git pull` brought in. A copy installed beforehand, even in target/release, is rebuilt or relinked over. A copy in install-target is never used.
- **Same commit, different sha.** This was seen on Central (2026-11-07: b31c9ab9 instead of the installed d93351b9) and on 2026-11-10 at three hosts:
  - Central cf655290 instead of the installed 7b460f25;
  - DL560 486f14ba instead of the installed 99f1808f;
  - Mac 17493c76.
  All built from the same source.
- **No cargo parent on Unix.** `cargo run` exec-replaces itself, so the TermAl process's parent is Greg's shell. That doesn't mean cargo wasn't used.
- **A host restarted for one landing moves to master HEAD.** `git pull` brings any host Greg restarts to origin/master, not to an older planned build. On 2026-11-10 the Mac was meant to stay on a6978c03 but was restarted.

After every restart, report for each host: pid, start time, checkout HEAD (read-only `git rev-parse HEAD`) and the binary file's sha with its mtime. Name the build as "Greg's git pull + cargo run --release at HEAD X". Record a sha as attested only when the file's mtime is earlier than the process start. On 2026-11-10 the DL560 and Mac files had mtimes about 4 minutes AFTER the start, which was unexplained at the time of writing.

Don't re-install a binary just to make the hash match; Greg's next start rebuilds it anyway.

Correction, 2026-11-10 15:55Z (Opus2 #5330, from Codex 6 #1039): the "about 4 minutes after start" mtime gap is EXPECTED on Linux and macOS, not suspicious.

On Unix, `cargo run` forks from Greg's shell, builds, then exec-replaces itself with the built binary. The PID and its start time therefore date from cargo's fork, before the build. The parent is the shell, the cmdline is target/release/termal, and /proc/PID/exe is the new build, not "(deleted)".

DL560 evidence:
- the clock was NTP-synced at +7 ms;
- the fingerprint dir was created at 15:31:38Z;
- the deps binary at 15:35:10Z is the same inode as target/release/termal and as /proc/135076/exe.
On Windows cargo can't exec, so cargo stays the parent (Central PID 51788).

The revised rule: on Unix, attest the running sha when /proc/PID/exe (or the deps hard link) equals the file and the deps fingerprint dir postdates the fork. On Windows, attest when the file's mtime predates the child's start. In both cases, name the source as the clean checkout HEAD read afterwards, because the binary embeds no commit.

REVISION 2026-11-16 (Fable2): the pid, start-time and /proc checks above are WITHDRAWN. Greg ruled on 2026-11-16 that process checks are not reliable, and they are not used (memory greg-no-process-checks-simple-procedures-2026-11-16). After a restart, verify from files only:
- the checkout HEAD with read-only `git rev-parse HEAD`, and that the checkout is clean;
- the sha256 and mtime of target/release/termal.exe, where an mtime after the last install shows Greg's rebuild;
- that the host answers API or mailbox calls.
Name the build "Greg's git pull + cargo run --release at HEAD X, sha Y".
First use: restart of 2026-11-16, HEAD 5537064c, exe rebuilt at 16:47:30Z, sha e3575f78 (installed copy a99d3f00, same source).
